overview: Unlike the simple digital IR obstacle sensor, the GP2Y0A21 gives an actual analog distance reading using triangulation: an internal IR emitter and a position-sensitive detector calculate distance from the angle light returns at, which makes it far less fooled by a target's color or reflectivity than a simple reflectance sensor. The catch is that its output voltage-to-distance relationship is distinctly non-linear (roughly an inverse curve, not a straight line), so converting the analog reading into a distance in centimeters requires a formula or lookup table from the datasheet rather than simple linear scaling.
simpleSummary: An analog distance sensor that's less fooled by an object's color than simpler IR sensors.

specifications.outputType: Analog voltage, inversely (non-linearly) related to distance
specifications.current: ~30 mA (has a distinctive spiky current draw pattern)

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.gotcha: The current draw has sharp periodic spikes as part of its internal measurement cycle — add a decoupling capacitor close to the sensor if readings look noisy.

pinMap.name: Vo
pinMap.function: Analog output voltage, inversely related to distance — higher voltage means closer object.
pinMap.gotcha: The voltage-to-distance curve is non-linear — don't scale it linearly, use the datasheet's conversion formula or a lookup table, or readings will be wrong except near the calibration point.

useCases.title: Obstacle-avoiding robot with distance-aware slowing
useCases.scenario: Slow down proportionally as an obstacle gets closer, rather than a simple stop/go response.

useCases.title: Cliff/edge detection
useCases.scenario: Mounted facing down, detect a sudden increase in measured distance indicating a table edge or stairs.

oftenConfusedWith: VL53L0X (laser ToF, much higher precision, digital I2C output)
oftenUpgradedTo: VL53L0X/VL53L1X for higher precision and a simpler linear digital reading
